title: Over any commutative ring and for arbitrary alpha,beta, all pathless representatives of one subdivision-algebra coset have the same image under x_(i,j) mapped to t_i
author: Darij Grinberg
work: t-Unique Reductions for Mészáros's Subdivision Algebra
source_version: Official SIGMA 14 (2018) article 078, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2018.078; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
difficulty_reason: Pathless straightening is not confluent and the evaluation map does not annihilate the relation ideal on arbitrary polynomials. The author overcomes both obstructions with an auxiliary Laurent-series realization and a nonmultiplicative coefficient map that becomes multiplicative on carefully selected source/sink subalgebras. Combining those restrictions with an injective formal substitution proves uniqueness uniformly over arbitrary commutative coefficient rings.

source_check.note: The complete original Theorem 2.7 and all author Sections 3.1–3.9 proof are retained over any commutative coefficient ring. The bounded-support Laurent-series algebra, continuous nonmultiplicative B, injective substitution E, source/sink adequate subalgebras and pathless-monomial compatibility are supplied in full as new core. The source expressly leaves the explicit three-generator substitution and elementary adequate-monomial multiplicativity checks as bounded algebra checks; these are preserved without a generated reproof. Nonconfluent pathless outputs need not be identical and D does not annihilate the ideal on arbitrary inputs. The independent forkless Groebner/basis result and symmetric appendix are not counted. proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The complete Theorem2.7 proof Sections3.1-3.9 was read, with all operator constructions and local support lemmas. The author embeds the defining relation ideal into a bounded-support Laurent-series algebra, constructs a continuous linear positive/negative-exponent map B that is not globally multiplicative, and an injective formal substitution E. For each pathless monomial the source proves a source/sink partition S that makes the restriction B_S multiplicative and identifies E*D with B*A. Injectivity then proves independence among all congruent pathless outputs. Proposition3.5 leaves only substitution of its explicit three-generator relation to a straightforward calculation;3.14 leaves the explicit monomial multiplicativity check to the reader. These are bounded algebra checks, while the entire nonconfluent-reduction core is supplied. The forkless Groebner-basis theorem is not selected separately.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem2.7 for any commutative ring k,alpha,beta in k and positive integer n. X=k[x_(i,j),1<=i<j<=n], J generated by x_(i,j)*x_(j,k)-x_(i,k)*(x_(i,j)+x_(j,k)+beta)-alpha. For a fixed p, every pathless polynomial q congruent to p modulo J has the same D(q), with D(x_(i,j))=t_i. Pathless means a linear combination of monomials with no x_(i,j)*x_(j,k) divisor for i<j<k. This does not assert uniqueness of q itself or D(q)=D(p), and no forkless-basis neighbor is counted.
